items.title: Worldkiln AI knowledge
items.summary: Choose Web for current documentation or Catalogue for engine-verified creator workflows. Browse one level at a time.

items.title: Web documentation
items.summary: Current Aeowun documentation is advisory; engine source and validator remain authoritative. No internet request occurs by opening this branch.

items.title: Search the current website
items.summary: Use search_live_aeowun_docs with a narrow topic (for example 'Actor navigation callbacks'); it returns titles/paths only, never full pages.
items.notes: Next: choose ONE result and pass its PATH to read_live_aeowun_doc. Do not fetch unrelated pages.

items.title: Search the offline index
items.summary: Use search_aeoscript_docs for engine/source-backed facts and indexed official references; use read_aeoscript_doc with a returned ID to dive into one page.
items.notes: Prefer source-backed examples to historic website snippets. The website may describe a different public release.

items.title: Creator catalogue
items.summary: Choose a topic to see its concepts and next-step options. Only an individual example page contains full code; nothing is bulk-injected.
items.notes: Use the examples as patterns, not guarantees of Play-mode behavior.

items.title: UI authoring and runtime UI
items.summary: Worldkiln offers editor-authored UI and runtime elements built with AeoScript. Script UI handles can be created, found by stable key, given properties and click callbacks.
items.notes: Authoring defines a saved document in the UI workspace; runtime changes are Play-session state. Ui elements include Panel, Text, Button. Choose a specific branch below.

items.title: Build a UI panel at runtime
items.summary: A global AeoScript can create runtime Panel and Text handles. Configure anchors, dimensions, colors and text via handle properties.
items.notes: Run in a project Global script. This example creates runtime-only elements, not an authored UI asset. Coordinates and sizes use screen-space units.
items.code:
const viewport = ui.get_viewport_size()
const panel = ui.new("Panel")
panel.key = "runtime_status"
panel.anchor = "TopLeft"
panel.position = [18, 18]
panel.size = [260, 64]
panel.color = [0.05, 0.05, 0.06, 0.9]
const title = ui.new("Text")
title.key = "runtime_status_text"
title.position = [30, 30]
title.size = [230, 24]
title.text = "Ready"

items.title: Use an authored UI element
items.summary: An authored UI document uses stable element keys. AeoScript can look up the element instead of creating a duplicate.
items.notes: First create and name the UI element in the UI Authoring workspace. Call ui.find(key) to find an element in the default document; ui.find(document_key, key) for a specific document.

items.title: Runtime Button and click behavior
items.summary: Button handles support on_click anonymous functions; do not wire clicks by changing a Text label or inventing ui.on_clicked.
items.notes: Call this from a Global script; event callback changes runtime UI only.

items.title: Responsive sizing and anchored elements
items.summary: Use ui.get_viewport_size() to inspect the runtime viewport; set valid named anchors and adapt positions/sizes as needed.
items.notes: Runtime element position and size are two-number arrays; color is four numbers [r,g,b,a]. Authored UI and runtime UI are separate creation workflows.

items.title: Navigation / walkability
items.summary: Navigation uses a bounded walkability grid sampled from supporting Cells and Terrain, not an exposed polygon-navmesh AeoScript builder. Actor navigation requires valid character control, walkable surfaces and reachable destinations.
items.notes: NavMesh bounds and slope/step/water settings belong in the editor Navigation panel. Calling navigate_to does not create walkable geometry. Navigation is BETA; do not claim reaching a destination without Play tests.

items.title: Configure NavMesh bounds
items.summary: Create/adjust NavMesh Bounds Volumes in the Navigation editor panel, then check walkability/debug visualization; configure max slope, step height and water-depth limits there.
items.notes: There is NO general navmesh.bounds() or navmesh.generate() AeoScript API. Existing solver samples grid cells within configured bounds; navigation snapshots may need regeneration after terrain changes.

items.title: Actor patrol with callback transitions
items.summary: Actor-attached Modules can access their owning Actor through self.parent. navigate_to accepts a destination basket [x,y,z], optional speed, and stop distance. Callbacks drive route legs.
items.notes: Attach this Module to a character-backed Actor. Replace example coordinates with reachable scene locations. Callbacks are a behavior contract; parsing does not prove the walkable route exists.

items.title: Track path success vs failure
items.summary: The navigation request indicates whether navigation starts. Completion/failure callbacks are the actual outcome; do not classify a point good from navigate_to() alone.
items.notes: A point recorded on finished is not necessarily permanently reachable if the scene changes. Example destinations are placeholders.

items.title: Cancel or inspect Actor navigation
items.summary: Actor handles have cancel_navigation() and is_navigating(). Cancelling navigation is different from reporting an unreachable path.
items.notes: Check whether the Actor is a character-backed navigable entity before calling. Player namespace supports separate controls and should not be mistaken for Actor handles.

items.title: Player scripts and controls
items.summary: Player Scripts attach to the runtime Player Actor through Project Explorer/Player Scripts, not a global playerscripts namespace. The built-in player namespace controls horizontal velocity, facing and animation.
items.notes: Use player.controller for the primary controller Module when available. Player-bound scripts differ from normal global scripts and Actor Modules.

items.title: Move and animate the Player
items.summary: Use player.set_horizontal_velocity(vx,vz), set_facing_direction(dx,dz), select_animation(name), is_grounded and apply_vertical_impulse.
items.notes: This demonstrates an explicit control request; a real controller calculates vx/vz from input and updates it. Do not create duplicate controllers by default.
items.code:
player.set_horizontal_velocity(2.0, 0.0)
player.set_facing_direction(1.0, 0.0)
player.select_animation("Walk")

items.title: Reference Player controller Module
items.summary: Player Scripts are attached via Explorer. The player.controller property points to the primary controller Module; player.find(name) can locate player-attached modules if available in the runtime.
items.notes: Accessing a module does not itself move the player. Do not invent a global playerscripts object.

items.title: Character grounded / jump
items.summary: Player character APIs include is_grounded() and apply_vertical_impulse(impulse). Use a gameplay/input condition before triggering a jump.
items.notes: Only character-backed player controllers respond. Calling each frame without input will repeatedly request jumps.

items.title: Actors, identity and attachments
items.summary: Actors are first-class authored or runtime objects distinct from Cells. Actor handles expose transforms, package, attributes and (on character-backed Actors) navigation and animation.
items.notes: Authored Actor IDs are persistent; names need not be unique. Prefer an Actor ID for instance-specific operations. An attached Module uses self.parent.

items.title: Actor-attached Module pattern
items.summary: Attach a Module from project Explorer or the AI attach_actor_script tool; top-level Module code runs in the attached context. self.parent is the Actor, not the Module instance.
items.notes: Do not use entity {...} lifecycle as a substitute for Actor Module attachment. Moving self is incorrect; call the supported Actor method on self.parent.
items.code:
const actor = self.parent
actor.set_position(1, 2, 3)
debug.log(actor.name())

items.title: Find authored Actors by identity
items.summary: Use proj.find(name) for a project-scoped Actor lookup; duplicate names are possible. A global find() is legacy.
items.notes: Check for nil if the named Actor is absent. Actor name is not a unique persistent reference.

items.title: Transform an Actor
items.summary: Actor.set_position takes three numeric arguments, not a basket. translate likewise takes x,y,z; navigation instead takes a destination basket.
items.notes: set_position teleports and is not pathfinding. Use navigate_to for walkable movement when a character/nav surface supports it.
items.code:
const guard = self.parent
guard.translate(0, 0, 1)
guard.set_position(3, 1, 7)

items.title: Cells versus Actors
items.summary: Cells are world/scene elements (Blocks, FxBlocks, Lights, emitters and other types). Actors are separately indexed scene objects and can have character/navigation behavior. Cells do not automatically expose Actor locomotion.
items.notes: Use cell.get(id), cell.exists(id), cell.new(type), and cell.delete(handle) for supported runtime Cell operations. Runtime changes do not overwrite authored project data.

items.title: Create a runtime Cell
items.summary: cell.new creates supported Cell types in the active Play world, not a saved editor asset. Configure the returned Cell handle using its supported properties.
items.notes: Confirm the accepted Cell type before creating. This example uses a Light Cell; placement and lighting require scene checks.

items.title: Read an existing Cell
items.summary: cell.get(id) returns a Cell handle or nil; cell.exists checks whether it exists. This differs from proj.find for Actor objects.
items.notes: Replace 42 with a real Cell ID from the project. The Cell may not be loaded or present in Play.

items.title: AeoScript Modules, files and state
items.summary: Module files live in scripts/ (reusable) or playerscripts/ (attached to Player). Modules own their own top-level state per runtime instance and may expose functions for callers.
items.notes: References use the scripts dotted path with .aeo suffix; importing a Module does not magically attach it to an Actor. Module names/files must exist.

items.title: A stateful reusable Module
items.summary: A Module's top-level typed variables persist for that runtime module instance. Functions called by another script can mutate declared state.
items.notes: Save this as scripts/counter.aeo. A separate caller uses scripts.counter.aeo (see Caller path). Not automatically persisted across Play sessions.

items.title: Call a reusable Module
items.summary: Reference an existing Module by path; its exported functions are callable. Files under scripts/ are different from player-attached scripts.
items.notes: Prerequisite: scripts/counter.aeo must exist. This is an example of project-bound module resolution; no script is created by this call.
items.code:
const counter = scripts.counter.aeo
counter.bump()
debug.log(counter.read_count())

items.title: AeoScript language patterns
items.summary: AeoScript uses newline-separated statements with no semicolons. New mutable variables require a type annotation; const declares immutable bindings. Baskets use len(), not JavaScript .length.
items.notes: Do not assume JavaScript, Lua or Python syntax. Bare assignments are reassignments only; undeclared names fail static validation and runtime.

items.title: Explicit variables and reassignment
items.summary: Declare mutable variables with a typed annotation. Use const for immutable bindings. Assignments to an undeclared name are invalid.
items.notes: `var name` and `let name` are not AeoScript syntax; a global bare name = value does not declare it.
items.code:
const limit = 10
speed: number = 5
speed = speed + 1
debug.log(speed, limit)

items.title: Basket collection length and append
items.summary: AeoScript baskets use .len() and .insert(index,value), not .length or JavaScript push().
items.notes: An index at basket.len() appends a new element. The basket must be mutable to rebind; contents may be changed through supported methods.
items.code:
points: basket = [[0, 0, 0]]
points.insert(points.len(), [4, 0, 8])
debug.log("Stored:", points.len())

items.title: Fire custom events
items.summary: Use event.fire(name, ...) to publish a named event; `on` declarations listen for custom events. Global on start() is not an automatic startup listener.
items.notes: Ordinary top-level Global statements execute at Play start. Refer to source event test for exact behavior.

items.title: Yielding wait in running script
items.summary: AeoScript uses wait(seconds) to yield in a resumable fiber. Do not assume a standalone `fn update(dt)` is automatically invoked on a Module.
items.notes: Always make loops yield; a tight while true without wait can stall runtime work.

items.title: Save data versus runtime module state
items.summary: A typed Module variable holds Play-session state; use save.get/save.set/save.commit for persistent data where supported.
items.notes: Persistence is project/game-specific. Do not equate an attached script variable with world.dat or an authored project property.

items.title: Player movement vs Actor navigation
items.summary: The player scripting namespace exposes velocity, facing, grounded and animation controls, but does not currently expose player.navigate_to(). NPC Actor handles have navigate_to() when character/pathfinding setup supports it.
items.notes: For automatic player travel, use a supported controller/Actor API if the engine exposes one in that context, or implement input/steering in a Player Script; do not invent player.navigate_to() or claim that a velocity command has verified pathfinding.
items.code:
player.set_horizontal_velocity(0.0, 2.0)
player.set_facing_direction(0.0, 1.0)
player.select_animation("Walk")

items.title: When to use Cells versus Actors
items.summary: Cells are engine-managed scene components such as blocks, effects, lights and emitters. Actors are distinct authored or runtime entities with identities, packages and potential character/navigation controls.
items.notes: Use cell.new(type) for a runtime Cell; choose imported Actors from the asset library or use the editor Actor tool for authored Actor objects. For scripts: Actor-attached Modules use self.parent; legacy Cell script bindings have a separate entity contract. Neither a Cell nor an Actor is interchangeable with the Player Script attachment list.
